sentences.japanese: 闘技場の下には、サメたちの牢獄があった。
sentences.reading: とうぎじょうの したには、サメたちの ろうごくが あった。
sentences.romaji: Togijo no shita ni wa, same-tachi no rogoku ga atta.
sentences.english: Beneath the arena, there was a prison where the sharks kept captives.
sentences.note: 下には sets the location: 'beneath...' or 'under...'

sentences.japanese: その奥で、聞き覚えのある歌声が聞こえた...
sentences.reading: その おくで、ききおぼえの ある うたごえが きこえた...
sentences.romaji: Sono oku de, kikioboe no aru utagoe ga kikoeta...
sentences.english: Deeper inside, he heard a voice, a song he knew too well...
sentences.note: 聞き覚えのある means something sounds familiar because you remember hearing it before.

sentences.japanese: そこには、姉ちゃんがいた...！
sentences.reading: そこには、ねえちゃんが いた...！
sentences.romaji: Soko ni wa, nee-chan ga ita...!
sentences.note: いた is the past tense of いる, used for people and living things.

sentences.english: Rio!? You should not be here!
sentences.note: 来ちゃだめ is casual speech for 来てはだめ, 'you must not come.'

sentences.japanese: 姉ちゃんを必ず助ける！
sentences.reading: ねえちゃんを かならず たすける！
sentences.english: I swear I will save you!

vocabulary.note: A dramatic word for a jail or dungeon.
Used for the back or depth of a place.
Often used in 聞き覚えがある, 'sounds familiar.'
歌 plus 声 means the sound of singing.
A casual contraction of 来てはだめ.

metadata.storyOrder: Rio reaches the prison beneath the arena and finds his sister.
